subject: Clarify DPA: audit-log export, retention windows, and derivative/no-train confirmation
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@novumhealth.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarification on DPA: logs, retention, and model training

Hi Avery,

Thanks for the demo last week — Novum's security team wants a couple of clarifications before we proceed to procurement. Can you confirm the following items for the DPA/addendum: 

1) Audit log export: do you provide an auditable export of request logs (timestamped requests, request_id, model version, token counts, redactable input/output) in a machine-readable format? If yes, can you share the spec and a sample CSV (sanitized)?

2) Retention windows: what are the default retention periods for raw request logs and for derivative artifacts (embeddings, prompt/response snapshots)? Can these be shortened/pinned per-customer?

3) No-train/opt-out: Novum requires a firm no-training/no-model-improvement commitment for data processed under our agreement. Do you have standard DPA language (or an addendum) that commits to not using customer data to improve models, and can you bind your subprocessors to the same restriction?

4) Ownership: we need explicit language that Novum retains ownership of prompts and responses and that Redwood will not claim derivative rights to customer outputs.

We're also attaching our security questionnaire. Procurement would like this answered this week if possible.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if that helps.

Best,
Marta Ruiz
Senior Privacy Counsel, Novum Health
(attachment: Novum_Security_Questionnaire.pdf)
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@novumhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarification on DPA: logs, retention, and model training

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Karthik (legal) and Monica (product/compliance). Below are preliminary answers; Karthik will follow up with contract language and a draft addendum.

Audit logs: yes — we can produce an export including request_id, timestamp (UTC), model_version, region, customer_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, and a SHA256 hash of input/output payloads (we do not export raw PII by default). We generate exports in CSV/JSONL and can provide a sanitized sample. See attached spec for field names and formats.

Retention: default log retention is 30 days for raw request payloads; hashed metadata and usage aggregates are retained longer for billing/analytics. Embeddings and prompt/response snapshots are retained by default for 30 days but can be shortened or configured to zero retention for customers with an opt-out. We can regionally pin storage (EU residency) under Redwood Private/Dedicated if required.

No-train/opt-out: we offer a No-Train Addendum that prevents Redwood and our subprocessors from using customer inputs or outputs to improve models. We will bind primary subprocessors (inference fleet, cloud storage) to the same commitments where contractually possible. There are rare edge cases (emergency security telemetry) we can carve out and document operationally; we'll include explicit language in the addendum.

Ownership: we can confirm Novum retains ownership of prompts and outputs. Redwood requests only a limited license to provide the service (operate, store, and transmit the data), and the No-Train Addendum removes rights to use data for model improvements.

Next steps: 
- Karthik will circulate a draft No-Train Addendum and a redline of the DPA.
- We'll attach a sanitized sample audit CSV and the export spec (see attached).
- If helpful, Monica can schedule a 30-minute call with your security/infra team to walk the export format.

I'll send the sample outside this thread in case procurement prefers a separate channel.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood-audit-export-spec.pdf)
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@novumhealth.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@novumhealth.com
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarification on DPA: logs, retention, and model training

Thanks Avery — that helps. Attaching our completed questionnaire; you'll see follow-ups inline. Two quick clarifications from the procurement/security side: 

- We need an example audit log CSV with one sanitized row so our SIEM team can validate ingestion (timestamp format, delimiter, field order). Can you provide that?

- Are embeddings stored in a way that they could be inadvertently used for training? We want technical confirmation (config flags, encryption at rest, separation of trainable stores).

- For 'ownership of outputs', procurement wants sample DPA text that states 'Customer retains all intellectual property rights in customer inputs and outputs; Provider shall not assert derivative rights or use outputs for model training.' If you can provide a one-paragraph sample clause we can insert into our PO, that would accelerate sign-off.

Procurement is on a tight schedule — ideally we get the CSV sample and draft clause by EOD tomorrow.

Appreciate it,
Marta
(attachment: Novum_Security_Questionnaire.pdf)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@novumhealth.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarification on DPA: logs, retention, and model training

Marta — thanks for the questionnaire and the follow-ups. Quoting your asks above and responding inline: 

> We need an example audit log CSV with one sanitized row

Attached is a one-row sanitized sample and the export field spec (CSV columns: request_id,timestamp_utc,model_version,region,customer_id,tokens_in,tokens_out,input_sha256,output_sha256). Sample uses RFC3339 timestamps and comma delim. Link to sample: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/novum-audit-sample-csv

> Are embeddings stored in a way that they could be inadvertently used for training?

Technical confirmation: embeddings and prompt/response snapshots are stored in customer-scoped object stores by default and are encrypted at rest with KMS keys. When a customer requests No-Train, we programmatically mark those stores with no-model-improvement flags and exclude them from any training/aggregation pipelines; subprocessors with access to those stores are contractually prohibited from using the data to update models. For extra assurance we can: (a) set retention to 0 days (ephemeral) for embeddings, (b) maintain an operations audit trail of any access, and (c) provide a scoped HMAC on exported vectors in the sample if you prefer.

> Provide a sample DPA clause stating customer ownership and no-derivative rights

Proposed (sample) clause: "Customer Data" means all data, content, prompts and outputs that Customer or its end users transmit to the Services. Customer retains all right, title and interest in Customer Data. Provider (Redwood Inference) and its subprocessors shall not use Customer Data to develop, improve, or train any models or datasets, and shall not assert any ownership or derivative rights over Customer Data or Customer Outputs, except to the limited extent necessary to provide the Services.

Operational items we commit to include in the No-Train Addendum: 
- Binding No-Train language for Provider and primary subprocessors.
- Audit log export spec and a guaranteed export delivery window (within 72 hours of request).
- Per-customer retention configuration and region pinning options.
- Evidence bundle: sample export, an ops runbook describing the 'no-train' flag path, and a signed attestation for subprocessors.

Attachments: no-train-addendum-draft.docx (draft language), redwood-audit-export-spec.pdf, sanitized-audit-sample.csv.

If that looks good I'll circulate the addendum for signature (DocuSign link included in related links). Monica — can you schedule a 30-minute walkthrough with Novum's infra team?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
General Counsel, Redwood Inference
(attachment: no-train-addendum-draft.docx)
